newsitem.title: DENMARK: Positive Danish bonds up a little after U.S. rises.
newsitem.headline: Positive Danish bonds up a little after U.S. rises.

text.p: Danish bond prices were slightly higher on Wednesday, bolstered by Wall Street gains, with dealers seeing the positive undertone continuing.
"We could see the 10-year yield gap with Germany narrow further today. If tomorrow's U.S. 2nd quarter GDP data and Friday's July NAPM are good, the positive trend will continue," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.01 point from the opening at 114.55, yielding 5.80 percent, with the upcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark 0.06 higher at 107.70, with yield at 5.98 percent.
Turnover in the tone-setting 2006 and 2007 papers was 2.1 billion and 1.6 billion crowns respectively.
The 2006's September future rose 0.30 point to 114.12 with 332 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.17 point to 93.00.
The crown traded at 3.8078 per mark at 1150 GMT. The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed one basis point to 48.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling a total of 450 million crowns worth of seven percent 2024 and 2007 bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
